evidence.caption:
you can delete the “sorry to bother you” part 😂

and the “i know you already explained this” part. you’re allowed to understand something while we’re on the phone and then hang up and go… wait.

sometimes you don’t realize what you’re unsure about until someone asks how the house stuff is going and you try to explain it out loud.

text me. even if all you have is a screenshot with “???” underneath. we can start there.

i talk about this stuff every day. you’re buying a home while you also have work tomorrow and still haven’t figured out dinner. i’m expecting questions.

and if i explain something and you’re still lost, please tell me. i can try another way. you don’t have to politely let me finish and then go ask google what i meant.

evidence.text: This is the register. This is so good! I love this. This is it!

We got here by giving the buyer a real conversational reply and letting Jen’s humor come through in how she responds. I’ll capture what made this caption work, then develop three new on-screen-text and caption pairs with different jobs: recognition, comparison, and reassurance.

Yes—the thing to preserve is a repeatable way of producing the work, with this caption as a concrete standard. It needs to accept either a topic or research, find the human situation, and develop the on-screen text and caption together. I’m using the Source-to-Skill-System workflow to build that reusable flow locally, with Jen’s voice as one specific application and checks that catch a return to generic copy.
